confirmedHigh.title: River water plane terminates in rectangular sawtooth teeth against sky/far bank

med.title: Paver texture repeat: identical chevron chip marches in straight dotted trails
med.evidence: 2x crop shows the same small dark check-mark blemish recurring once per tile row in the same texture column, forming a straight dotted line receding to the horizon (marks near (600,480),(575,545),(515,585),(490,620),(465,690) original coords); a second parallel trail runs at x~1600-1700. med.suggested_direction: Edit the chevron chip out of the paver albedo tile (or reduce its contrast), or break repetition with UV rotation/offset variation per tile region.

med.title: Hairline polygonal seams crisscross the glossy water surface

med.suggested_direction: Make water band overlaps coplanar within a single material (weld or merge bands into one mesh for the visual layer), or increase overlap and remove the per-seg z-stagger on the render mesh so joints stop catching the glossy reflection.

med.title: Levee slope reads as stacked flat plates: overlapping rims, stepped skyline, glitter-chip 'grass' with specular bloom
med.evidence: Crop: knife-edge plate rim runs diagonally (1290,570)-(1470,900) with a second plate floating over it top-right; grass material is a confetti-chip pattern with a large white specular bloom (frac lum>0.9 = 1.9% inside the box, peak 0.984). Same construction shows terraced sawtooth skyline in pt_noon_bank_oblique.png top-left (85,283)-(390,330) and hard flat facet creases across the slope.
med.why_unreal: Grass is matte; a broad white sheen plus terrazzo-like chip texture reads as green-painted sparkly concrete boards, and the overlapping plate edges with stepped silhettes expose the slope as loose stacked slabs rather than a continuous earth bank.
med.suggested_direction: Kill/lower specular+roughness response on the slope grass material at grazing angles, use the lawn grass shader of the flat berms, and hide band rims by butting slope bands flush (or adding a thin soil trim) so no plate edge or terrace step silhouettes against sky.

med.title: Cycle-track white lane markings bleed onto the grass terraces beside the stair
med.evidence: 3x crop: a white painted wedge lies on the grass terrace, ending abruptly at the terrace knife-edge; second segment at (0,690)-(90,745) and a mirrored one on the right side (1500-1660, 590-630). med.suggested_direction: Clip the lane-marking strip prims to the track band extent (same s-range as the track), or drop the marking z below the grass band z where the track is cut by the stair corridor.

med.title: Leaf-litter drift beds read as raised slabs with vertical cut faces

med.title: Trail dead-ends into featureless gray void through hedge gap
med.evidence: Crop (640,340,1100,640): mean RGB (0.539,0.539,0.536) — max channel spread 0.003, zero texture from ground level to sky; the trail leads directly into this flat neutral field; hedge wall terminus shows an unlit near-black end face (pt_noon_preset_h0.9_d2.png ~1008,300,1035,360).

med.suggested_direction: Add far-side backdrop content (tree line / terrain roll / haze gradient with ground detail) behind the hedge gap, and cap the hedge terminus with a lit return face.

med.evidence: Crop (950,720,1470,910): disc is constant flat gray (RGB 0.600,0.597,0.602, no metal/relief texture at ~400px width), sits several cm proud with a smooth rim ring, and the paving joint lines run underneath it — no collar or cutout; same in pt_noon_preset_h1.8_d10.png (~985,620,1115,660).

med.title: Stepping-stone gaps render as pitch-black open slots
med.evidence: Slit at y=900 measures 8 px wide (x 833-840) with lum < 0.05, min 0.003 at noon; two parallel diagonal slots in the box. Same defect from grazing angle in pt_noon_grazing_edge.png (560,640,1780,760): ~8 wedge-shaped notches along tread edges, lum min 0.008 while surrounding treads read 0.57 mean.

med.evidence: Autocorrelation of the detrended path strip (880,640,1060,800) peaks at lag 86-94 px with r=0.20; zoom crop shows identical mottle rectangles tiled in rows. med.title: Manhole is a flat featureless grey decal
med.evidence: Uniform grey ellipse with no rim ring, no cover pattern, no specular response; paver joints terminate at its edge, so it is a distinct surface, not a shadow. Recurs at pt_noon_preset_h0.9_d10.png (550,425,670,465) and pt_noon_preset_h0.3_d5.png (0,415,230,455).

med.suggested_direction: Swap the disc for a ringed cover texture (frame + patterned lid) or a shallow extruded prim with a metal material.

med.title: Duck canopy renders pastel pink vs declared brick red
med.evidence: Canopy top edge rgb (0.74,0.58,0.56) and shaded vertical leg rgb (0.59,0.49,0.48) give R/G ratio ~1.2, while PARAMS duck_top_color is (0.52,0.19,0.17), R/G 2.7. The wash-out appears on vertical faces too, so the known horizontal noon clipHi mechanism does not explain it.

med.title: Pure-black embankment plane beside the upper pond
med.evidence: Featureless black wedge between upper pond and plaza: 12% of box below lum 0.02, straight planar edges, zero detail. Ground view pt_noon_landing_return.png (900,150,1050,270): the stair crest zigzag is silhouetted against the same void (lum min 0.007, 12.3% below 0.02) at noon.

med.title: Retaining-wall crest melts/notches under RidgeCrest hedge crowns
med.evidence: 3x crop shows the wall's top edge dipping in scooped curved notches beneath each crown gap, with crown undersides punching below the coping line; a cone 'drip' hangs down the wall face at approx (1295,451)-(1307,465). Same artifact in pt_noon_preset_h1.8_d2.png at (1170,455)-(1430,495) including a stalactite-like spike at (1317,465)-(1335,487). The straight masonry crest line is visibly deformed under every crown.

med.suggested_direction: Raise the RidgeCrest crown base z (or push crowns behind the wall plane) so crown undersides stay above/behind the coping line; keep the crown band idiom itself (doctrine) untouched.

med.title: Lower-park ground is hard-edged rectangular dirt/grass patchwork
med.evidence: 3x crop shows distinct rectangles of dirt and grass materials meeting at razor-straight right angles with zero transition pixels: green grass rect approx (1780,140)-(1920,300) butted inside tan dirt bands (1745,150)-(1810,420). The same checkerboard patch grid is visible on the trail bands in pt_noon_preset_h1.8_d10.png around (700,555)-(1100,640) as parallel hard-edged brown strips.

med.title: Bus-shelter panels render near pure black in noon daylight
med.evidence: Shadow-side shelter panels measure mean lum 0.046 with 15.2% of pixels below 0.02 and 44.3% below 0.05 (max-channel), directly adjacent to sunlit pavement at ~0.6+. The same shelter reads as a black-silhouette box from the overview cut as well ((600,760)-(1000,1030)).

med.suggested_direction: Check the shelter panel material albedo (likely near-zero or untinted) and that it receives GI/ambient; a dark-gray tinted metal with albedo ~0.05-0.10 would resolve it.

Windows and bushes inside the band are barely distinguishable.

med.title: Spoil piles render as two smooth overlapping hemispherical domes
med.evidence: Crop (also pt_noon_preset_h1.8_d5.png 1490,400,1830,560 and h1.8_d10 1300,350,1650,530) shows exactly two clean spherical-cap silhouettes with fine sand-speckle texture; toe meets the slab at a steep near-vertical tangent, only tiny PileToe stones break the base. The GT-115(6) 3-lobe fix (docstring: 'crest/shoulder silhouette breaks instead of reading as one dome', repose 35-40 deg) does not read in pixels - the crest arc is a single unbroken curve.
med.why_unreal: Loose aggregate cannot hold a hemispherical profile (angle of repose 30-40 deg); the piles read as giant smooth pebbles / CG primitives, the exact 'smooth pebble' verdict the mounds already received in r2.
med.suggested_direction: Exaggerate lobe offsets/asymmetry so the silhouette visibly breaks, flatten sz further, and add granular clumping or a coarser aggregate normal map at the crest.

med.title: Footprint trail renders as ~1 m rectangular leaf-litter decal insets
med.evidence: Crop shows a sharply bounded parallelogram patch of leaf/gravel texture inset in the slab: boundary max horizontal gradient 0.44/px (razor 1-px edge), individual leaf shapes clipped mid-leaf at the straight border, and a continuous dark seam line along the edge. The trail of identical rectangles is visible marching toward the opening in pt_noon_preset_h0.9_d10.png (1000,420,1400,740). Patch length ~0.6-1.0 m (vs 0.3 m boot print) measured against the 1.5 m opening width in beauty_overview.
med.why_unreal: Spec says 8-15 footprints (+0.6 mm relief); what renders is a chain of meter-long sharp-edged leaf-litter rectangles on a broom-finished slab with no trees anywhere in the scene - they read as misplaced material decals or cut holes, not traffic wear.
med.suggested_direction: Replace the patch texture with a boot-tread/dust smear at 0.3 m scale, feather the decal alpha, and remove the leaf-litter content indoors.

med.title: Crushed-concrete debris renders as perfect cubes and spheres
med.evidence: Crop shows a debris fragment at the lip ring as a true cube (three faces, crisp 90-deg edges, uniform 2-3 mm speckle texture); pt_noon_preset_h0.3_d2.png (960,490,1060,580) and beauty_overview show companion fragments as perfect spheres. 46-fragment scatter per PARAMS debris block.
med.why_unreal: Crushed concrete is angular and irregular; geometric primitives (exact cubes, exact spheres) scattered as rubble read as untextured proxy props and undercut the construction-site story at the hazard lip.
med.suggested_direction: Swap the box/sphere prims for 2-3 irregular convex chunk meshes (or randomized scale/shear per axis plus rotation) keeping the existing no-overhang ring constraint.

med.title: Channel-bottom leaf litter renders as metallic gold coins
med.evidence: Crop shows ~20 perfect flat circular discs (~0.07-0.10 m vs the 0.5 m channel invert) in saturated gold/copper/amber with specular sheen, lum up to 0.84; two larger 0.5 m oval mounds carry an actual leaf-litter texture, making the disc proxies stand out. Same discs down the whole channel in pt_noon_preset_h0.9_d2.png (900,330,1010,1010).
med.why_unreal: Fallen leaves are irregular, matte, and desaturated brown; uniform bright circular discs read as scattered coins or bottle caps lining the drain - a casual close view breaks immediately.
med.suggested_direction: Replace the disc prims with leaf card meshes (irregular outline, matte brown-olive albedo, random flip/curl) or extend the existing leaf-mat texture treatment to the singles.

med.title: Power-line shadows render as razor-sharp pure-black slits in the lawn
med.evidence: Crop shows two collinear 3-6 px wide, ~470 px long straight black lines (lum 0.02-0.05 vs 0.55 lawn) with a jog between segments, tracking the overhead conductors. Meanwhile the same scene draws a soft 50%-dimming ~20 px band across the shoulder in pt_noon_grazing_low.png (400,855,1800,880) - two contradictory shadow languages for the same wire system.
med.why_unreal: A 1-2 cm wire ~8 m up cannot cast an umbra under a 0.5-deg sun - only a faint wide penumbra; full-black hairline slits read as open cracks or seam gaps in the terrain, not shadows.
med.suggested_direction: Give the sun its angular diameter (or thicken/soften shadow-casting on the conductor prims) so wire shadows wash out like the grazing_low band does.

med.title: Verge turf reads as a raised carpet slab with a black under-lip seam
med.evidence: Crop shows the turf layer terminating in a razor-straight lip over the channel headwall with (a) a continuous 1-3 px near-black gap line under the overhang running the full frame, and (b) the vertical cut face textured with the same lawn texture as the top (grass runs down the soil profile). Same read at pt_noon_preset_h0.3_d2.png (340,430,620,470).
med.why_unreal: A soil verge cut at a concrete channel shows a brown earth profile with ragged grass overhang; a green-faced, perfectly straight raised slab with a shadow slot underneath reads as artificial turf laid loose on the wall cap.
med.suggested_direction: Texture the turf-layer side face as soil, drop the layer flush onto the cap (kill the gap), and jitter the lip line slightly.

med.title: Tactile band splits into two rows around a dark floor-textured groove
med.evidence: Gain-boosted crop shows the two dot-block rows separated by a recessed strip carrying the bare platform floor texture; luminance profile at y=1000 dips to 0.037-0.08 across x 500-620 vs 0.13-0.33 on the plates, and the gap:row pixel ratio measures ~0.13-0.3 across cuts vs the declared 0.02/0.30 = 0.067 (PARAMS tactile gap=0.02). The groove runs the full platform length (pt_noon_edge_graze.png 930,500,1200,1080). The two rows also render in different tones - clean bright yellow vs grimed amber - reading as mismatched tile batches.
med.why_unreal: Korean platform warning blocks are laid contiguous; a continuous dark slot splitting the band reads as an open drainage channel or a laying error right at the safety strip, and the per-row tone jump reinforces the seam.
med.suggested_direction: Close the inter-row gap to the declared 2 cm (or butt the rows), and unify the two rows' texture wear (same UV offset/grime level) so the band reads as one installation.

low.title: Streetlight pole planted directly in front of bench centre
low.evidence: 3x crop (0,330)-(260,500): pole shaft x~110-137 occludes the bench seat mid-span; pole base ellipse lands at y~440-460, at the bench front-leg line. Second angle confirms: in pt_noon_beauty_overview.png the pole base (215,400)-(262,415) sits at the front edge of the bench body (102,325)-(330,415).
low.why_unreal: A lamp pole rising dead-centre in front of a bench seat (documented design clearance is only 0.50 m, scene01_campus_stairs.py streetlight note: pole line y 6.30 vs bench row y 7.10) blocks the sitters' knees; real plazas offset poles to bench ends. From both plaza camera angles it reads as the pole growing out of the bench.
low.suggested_direction: Shift the pole line x-coordinates half a module so poles align with bench gaps, or push the pole line 0.5-1.0 m further from the bench row; keep the equal-spacing rule by moving the whole line.

low.title: Benches straddle slope terraces with visibly tilted seats
low.evidence: 5x crop: the wooden bench stands mid-slope across a terrace crease (grass tone change behind it); the seat plane tilts visibly toward the river, rear legs on the upper band, front legs on the lower. The mirrored bench at (1350,745)-(1460,790) shows the same. Also seen in pt_noon_preset_h1.8_d5.png at (405,617)-(490,690).
low.why_unreal: Park benches are set level on a pad or the flat berm; a bench perched mid-slope with a sloping seat would not be usable and reads as scattered props.
low.suggested_direction: Move the two mid-slope benches onto the flat berm (crest walk shoulder or beach flat), or level them on a small gravel pad prim.

low.title: Charcoal paving band shows one-axis smeared texture
low.evidence: Crop (620,510,1310,660): the dark inlay band's texture detail runs purely horizontally (brushed-line striations, no cross grain), unlike the granular granite of surrounding slabs; band is neutral (RGB 0.641,0.638,0.640).
low.why_unreal: Stone paving has isotropic grain; a band where all detail streaks along one axis reads as a stretched UV, especially adjacent to correctly grained slabs.
low.suggested_direction: Fix the UV aspect on the granite_dark band strips (likely scaled only along the band length) or swap to the same granite texture at matched world scale.

low.title: Hairline joint arc on stage floor dead-ends mid-pavement
low.evidence: Crop (400,980,900,1050): a 1-2px dark arc (min lum 0.129) crosses the stage paving and terminates abruptly mid-floor at its west end rather than meeting a joint or edge.
low.why_unreal: Pavement joints run between construction edges; a crack that stops in the middle of a monolithic floor reads as a mesh boundary.
low.suggested_direction: Extend the stage-circle boundary ring to a closing edge or drop its z-offset so the seam is invisible.

low.title: Saturated red speck cluster on backdrop building facade
low.evidence: Strict red mask (r>0.55, r-max(g,b)>0.35) hits 5px in 2 clusters at (365-367,145-151) on the brick facade; no other saturated red exists in the scene's 13 cuts.

low.suggested_direction: Locate the red marker prim in the building kit (same family as the scene06 markers) and remove or hide it from render.

low.title: Roadway asphalt shows regular diamond-plate tiling seams
low.evidence: Crop (200,550,950,1050): the asphalt carries a regular criss-cross grid of diagonal seam lines repeating every ~80-100px (~2-3m world) across all lanes, same period everywhere; visible over the whole carriageway in the overview.
low.why_unreal: Asphalt is laid in lane-wide continuous mats with rare straight joints; a uniform diamond grid over the full road reads as a repeated texture tile.
low.suggested_direction: Likely covered by the queued lever-1 asphalt recalibration: raise texture world scale / decorrelate tiling (rotation-blend) so the repeat period exceeds the visible span.

low.title: Row of near-black tilted slabs half-buried at plaza/grass edge
low.evidence: Crop (1350,960,1560,1080) at 3x: five charcoal rectangular blocks (p1 lum 0.007, 2.6% of crop <0.02) sit along the herringbone-paving/grass boundary at irregular rotations, each partially overlapping the paving and partially sunk in grass.
low.why_unreal: Edge units (kerbs, seat blocks, step stones) follow the boundary line at consistent orientation; randomly rotated near-black boxes overlapping finished paving read as misplaced prims.
low.suggested_direction: Identify the prop row (planter/edging blocks) and either align them to the paving edge with consistent spacing or remove; brighten material so they read as stone, not void.

low.title: Taut seam line runs across south retaining wall face
low.evidence: A 3-4 px bar with top highlight and bottom shadow crosses the full masonry face diagonally until occluded by the boulder at x=390; the same line spans pt_noon_stone_rhythm.png (0,405,970,455) horizontally across the entire wall, cutting through block courses mid-block.
low.why_unreal: Reads as a stretched wire or a razor ledge floating on a stone wall — the seam between overlapping wall prisms ignores the block pattern, which real masonry cannot do.
low.suggested_direction: Make the two wall prisms flush (or recess the rear prism), or cover the junction with a coping course so the seam reads as an intentional string course.

low.title: Water surface is ripple-free, reads as resin floor
low.evidence: Water rgb mean (0.47,0.60,0.63); luminance variation is only a smooth gradient (std 0.092, no high-frequency component); the duck reflection is mirror-sharp and no sparkle or wave normal perturbation appears in any of the 6 water cuts; both waterlines are razor-straight.
low.why_unreal: A saturated uniform teal sheet with perfect mirror reflections reads as painted resin or pool paint, not lake water — and the waterline is this scene's only fixed drop anchor, so the material carries the judgment read.
low.suggested_direction: Add low-amplitude wave normals / roughness variation to soften reflections, keeping the waterline band legible.

low.title: Sunlit rigid straw-rod inside the shadowed under-deck cavity
low.evidence: 4x crop: a 1-3px wide perfectly straight bright rod spans diagonally from the deck rim board down to the ground inside the under-deck cavity; sampled rod pixels peak at lum 0.57 (mean of per-point max 0.13) against surrounding shadowed boards at mean lum 0.057 — 10x brighter than its environment. Length corresponds to roughly 1 m in world scale.
low.why_unreal: Reads as a rigid 1 m straw leaning at a perfect angle while catching full sun inside a fully shaded cavity — both the prop and its lighting are implausible.
low.suggested_direction: Remove or lay down the stray debris/blade instance under the deck rim (likely a VEG_DEBRIS instance at wrong scale); check for a sun light leak through the rim gap.

low.title: Ground at macro distance is a flat photo texture (no relief)
low.evidence: At ~0.3 m viewing distance the grass/leaf-litter ground is a single planar texture: color variance is healthy (std 0.14-0.17 per channel) but there is zero silhouette relief or parallax along leaf shapes — leaf outlines render as print on a flat plane while modeled 3D leaves exist elsewhere in the same frame (top edge).
low.why_unreal: Printed-tarp look at close range; a real litter band has 3D leaf edges and blade occlusion at 30 cm.
low.suggested_direction: Near h0.3 camera positions add instanced blades/leaf cards or displacement to the litter band (same quality gap family as the s13 micro_sd item in GT-107).

low.title: Street-tree crowns are untextured faceted spheres at close range
low.evidence: Crowns beside the deck are smooth flat-shaded green blobs with hard triangular facet creases catching light (clearly visible around (960,330)-(1200,560)); zero foliage albedo/normal detail at ~8-10 m. The same species rendered in pt_noon_overview.png sidewalk rows shows proper leafy texture, so this is an asset/LOD inconsistency, not a style choice.
low.why_unreal: Giant clay balls at eye level next to a detailed railing break material consistency; the trimmed-hedge doctrine covers box hedges, not creased untextured sphere crowns at close range.
low.suggested_direction: Swap the deck-adjacent crown assets to the leafy-textured variant used along the sidewalk, or add foliage albedo/normal to the crown material; geometry may stay.

low.title: Reed clumps are leafless uniform green dowels
low.evidence: Stalks render as constant-radius (r=0.022 per PARAMS) segmented cylinders with no leaf blades or seed heads, tilted at random angles up to the 9-degree spec, several crossing mid-air; at h0.9 distance they read as green plastic straws stuck in the cobble. Same read in pt_noon_bank_face.png (900,580)-(1550,800).
low.why_unreal: Real reeds/silver grass show tapering blades and plumes; bare rigid rods look like markers, not vegetation. Noted: this is the corpus-wide scene09/scene17 reed convention, so it is an asset-quality item, not a scene12 wiring bug.
low.suggested_direction: If the shared convention is ever revisited, add a simple blade/plume card per stalk (kept within the reed_selfcheck prim budget); per-scene fixes are not appropriate while the 21-scene convention stands.

low.title: Far-shore lawn reads as a green sheet floating on the water

low.why_unreal: Even a low floodplain shows a bank face or revetment sliver at the waterline; a zero-thickness green wedge on the horizon reads as a board laid on the water.
low.suggested_direction: Add a thin quay/bank fascia (0.3-0.5 m) under the far-shore lawn edge, matching the gray band already present behind the piers in pt_noon_broken_span.png.

low.title: Gray runner strips on driveway are textureless flat panels
low.evidence: Matched-distance comparison: gray strip lum sd 0.038 / hi-freq gradient 0.0050 vs adjacent brown coat sd 0.182 / hi-freq 0.0176 (3.5x); in pt_noon_preset_h0.3_d10.png at 1300,420-1500,560 hi-freq 0.0119 vs brown 0.0101 only from distance blur — near-field strip shows zero granularity while the brown urethane coat is strongly granular.

low.suggested_direction: Assign a subtle concrete micro-texture (matching the crest trench-drain gray family) to the two runner strips; keep albedo band compliance.

low.title: Giant arc-shaped sweep smear band across terrace flagstones

Faintly visible again at distance in pt_noon_preset_h1.8_d10.png y~620-660.

low.title: Castle-style crenellated parapet blocks on office building towers

low.title: Weed tufts sprouting through the middle of the statutory tactile band

low.suggested_direction: Exclude the tactile band footprint (both bands) from the weed scatter mask, or snap the tufts to the band's edge joints.

low.title: Healthy weed tufts mid-lane on marked levee roads, same asset repeated

low.title: Beach berm scarp is a laser-straight prism edge along the entire waterline

low.title: Green deck grain reads as corduroy/chenille fabric rather than urethane membrane
low.evidence: One-axis grooves at ~20 px pitch at 2 m grazing distance (~2.4 cm world pitch) with fibrous white wisps between dark grooves cover the entire deck in every h0.3/h0.9 cut; per-pixel saturation mean 0.40 with groove minima lum ~0.29 and ridge highlights ~0.84, giving a fabric-like sheen. low.suggested_direction: Reduce groove amplitude/contrast of the membrane detail normal (or enlarge detail scale) so only the declared 0.9-1.1 m roll seams read at grazing angles.

low.title: Twin backdrop masses are near-mirror windowless boxes with identical brick chimney stubs
low.evidence: Left (x150-880) and right (x1075-1810) masses have identical composition: blank brick face, one offset brick penthouse stub, one concrete stair cheek passing in front; zero door/window openings while brick courses fully resolve. Declared kind="backdrop" silhouettes, but they sit close enough that texture detail resolves.
low.why_unreal: Two mirror-copied blank brick warehouses framing a plaza reads as stage scenery; any real block this close would show at least a door, vents, or downspouts.
low.suggested_direction: Either push the blocks farther/haze them so texture stops resolving, or add 1-2 minimal openings and break the copy symmetry (different stub position/height already helps).

low.title: Manholes read as featureless near-black lenses sitting proud of the paving
low.evidence: Both discs (second at 1150,320,1310,350; also pt_noon_preset_h0.9_d10.png 595,478,775,520) render as uniform dark ellipses, mean lum 0.52-0.62 crop-wide but disc body ~0.13-0.2 with min 0.05, no cover pattern or metallic highlight at noon; at h0.3 grazing the disc shows a domed silhouette with a dark underside line, i.e. proud of the surface rather than flush.

low.suggested_direction: Flush the cover z to the paving, add the cover-pattern normal/roughness so noon sun produces highlights, and lighten the albedo toward worn cast iron (~0.25-0.3).

low.title: Manhole covers are perfectly featureless discs
low.evidence: Cover interior luminance 0.388 +/- 0.001 across a ~390px-wide disc (profile x690-710: constant 0.387-0.391); no cast pattern, pick holes or text. Seating is correctly flush (no proud side face; single bevel-highlight row 0.43-0.45 at the rim) — only the surface is blank.

low.suggested_direction: Give the manhole lid a normal/roughness pattern map or a low-cost concentric-ring displacement.

low.title: Manhole covers are featureless near-black discs
low.evidence: Cover top reads a constant 0.188 (profile x620-640: 0.187-0.191 over the full chord, std<0.002); near cover in pt_noon_approach.png (600,985)-(905,1080) has lum 0.13-0.19 with zero surface structure. Darkness itself is the documented cast-iron sRGB 0.02-0.06 convention (scene file line 330) and is not flagged; seating is flush with correct rim highlight.
low.why_unreal: With zero molded pattern or specular breakup the dark disc reads as a painted void rather than an iron lid — in a no-drop hard-negative this is the one prop that most needs to read as solid metal.
low.suggested_direction: Keep the dark albedo convention but add the cover pattern via normal/roughness map so micro-highlights break the silhouette.

low.title: Pure-black facet slot between ridge turf slabs above the left wall

Not explained by any known exposure mechanism (scene is sunlit noon).

low.suggested_direction: Close the gap between the two adjacent GT-126(c) turf slabs at that station (or fix the flipped/unlit side face) so the ridge silhouette is continuous.

low.title: Drain grate runs overlap with doubled slats and a blank wedge at the direction change

low.suggested_direction: Butt-join the two grate segments at the bend or insert a solid junction-box frame prim so the slat rhythm terminates cleanly on both sides.

low.title: Regular dot-grid patterning on the mid-plaza snow

The regularity follows the perspective grid, consistent with periodic show-through/texture repeat rather than random trampling (nearby foreground footprints are irregular by contrast).
low.why_unreal: Fresh trampled snow does not carry a uniform polka-dot lattice; at a glance the mid-ground reads as wallpaper repeat.
low.suggested_direction: Break the repeat (rotated/rescaled second octave on the snow albedo, or randomize the paver show-through mask amplitude) so the mid-zone loses the aligned dot grid.

low.title: Snow pile meets ground with a hard undercut and a black notch at the buried pole
low.evidence: 2.5x crop of the left pile: pure-black pixel cluster (lum ~0.004) exactly where the gray post enters the pile crest, and the pile's downhill base shows a hard dark undercut slot (196,712,300,772) where the squashed-sphere shell intersects the ground plane instead of feathering out; the same base condition shows on the left mounds in h0.9_d10 and h0.3_d10.
low.why_unreal: Plowed snow piles taper into the ground and pack around posts; an ellipsoid edge with a shadow slot underneath plus a black void at the pole junction reads as intersecting primitives.
low.suggested_direction: Add a base skirt/taper to the squashed-sphere pile cluster and a small snow collar where poles penetrate the piles.

low.title: Razor-straight tan seam lines cross the lawn
low.evidence: ~4 px perfectly straight tan line (strip RGB 0.416,0.407,0.297 vs surrounding grass 0.315,0.345,0.248) running from frame edge to the path; the same line appears in pt_noon_approach_walk.png (~y 430) and pt_noon_beauty_side.png. Matches the edge_break_w=0.20 break-up band (lines 145-146).
low.why_unreal: A 0.2 m perfectly straight dirt hairline across a mown lawn reads as a texture/geometry seam rather than wear or deposition.
